usefulness.use_case: Systems Programming & Embedded OS Kernel Call Stacks
usefulness.example: In mission-critical firmware, dynamic stack structures must strictly free every popped node to prevent kernel heap exhaustion.
usefulness.benefit: Intercepts memory leaks and pointer corruption before software is flashed to hardware.

usefulness.use_case: Automated Pointer Safety & Stack Underflow Triage
usefulness.example: When an empty stack receives POP or PEEK, the agent ensures the program safely outputs 'UNDERFLOW' without null pointer dereference crashes.
usefulness.benefit: Eliminates segmentation faults (0xC0000005) in student lab submissions.

usefulness.use_case: Modular Object-Oriented Architecture Verification in C
usefulness.example: Enforces separation of concerns across push(), pop(), and free_stack() helper functions rather than monolithic main() implementations.
usefulness.benefit: Instills industrial software design patterns in undergraduate engineers.

limitations.example: A student's stack program exits after 10 operations without triggering OS heap fragmentation that only manifests after millions of allocations.
limitations.mitigation: Execute fuzzing stress tests with 100,000+ random interleaved push/pop operations under ASan instrumentation.

limitations.example: GCC at -O3 may inline small node structs or optimize them into stack frames, potentially bypassing certain static heap checks.
limitations.mitigation: Evaluate submissions under both -O0 (raw pointer inspection) and -O2 (optimized safety).
